01 — Configurator

A 3D configurator that replaced the quotation process

Product design · Interaction design · React / Three.js · Shipped at KANA Furniture

Problem

Pricing custom furniture was the sales bottleneck: every serious inquiry needed a designer to estimate materials and hours, with days of back-and-forth before the customer saw a number. People lost interest in the wait.

What I did

Pushed the company toward modular product lines and designed a configurator where customers compose the piece in 3D and see the price instantly. Every option is wired to real BOMs and cut-lists, so the workshop can build exactly what the screen promises. Designed and built end-to-end, solo, with Claude Code as daily build partner.

Decisions & trade-offs

Config lives in one source-of-truth file so adding a product is data, not code. Rhino → glTF pipeline chosen over Fusion for native PBR materials. Cut scope ruthlessly: one product family first, alignment tooling before visual polish.

// the configurator in motion — Sandouq by KANA: pick doors, price updates live
// step 5 of 7: every door option is a door we actually make
What changed

Pricing stopped being a conversation and became a number on screen. The workshop receives production-ready specs instead of interpreting chat messages — and the company reoriented its product strategy around this way of selling.

02 — Operations

An operations dashboard the board actually reads

Internal product · Design system · Data design · Python / Google Apps Script

Problem

The factory ran on scattered spreadsheets. Assembling a monthly picture of the company took days of manual collection, and the answer depended on who compiled it.

What I did

Designed and built a reporting product: one model pulling inventory movement, project activity, and costs — revenue imputed from material consumption, the most honest signal in a workshop. The monthly board audit generates itself: dashboard, KPI comparisons, and a written narrative auto-generated in Arabic and English.

Design notes

Built its own small design system — editorial typography, restrained palette, charts designed for non-technical readers. The words are part of the interface: a report you can read, not just a wall of numbers.

// daily activity per project, editorial design system — client legend cropped for confidentiality
What changed

The monthly picture became a routine instead of a project. Leadership discusses numbers rather than assembling them — and strategic calls, including the modular pivot, were argued from this reporting.

03 — Identity

A brand identity drawn from geometry the products already had

Brand design · Visual identity · Product pages

Problem

A workshop moving from bespoke commissions to product lines needs a face — something ownable, systematic, and honest about what the products are.

What I did

Built the identity on Islamic geometric design: a Square Kufi logotype that aligns with the geometric drawer faces of the furniture itself. Extended it into product landing pages and sales material, including a designer trade program one-pager.

Why it works

The identity isn't decoration on top of the products — it's derived from them. Same grid, same geometry, one system from logo to drawer face to web page.

// square kufi logotype, drawn on the unit grid
// the system in product: table configurator with live quotation
What changed

KANA has one visual language from logo to product to page — a brand a small workshop can actually maintain, because it's a system, not a style.

04 — AI Pipeline

Product photography without a studio: an AI catalogue pipeline

AI workflow design · ComfyUI · ControlNet · IP-Adapter · Run locally

Problem

A product-line catalogue needs consistent, styled imagery for every variant — studio photography for each one is slow and expensive at workshop scale.

What I did

Built a local pipeline on ComfyUI: ControlNet holds the product's exact geometry, IP-Adapter carries the brand's visual style, inpainting handles set dressing. Renders and real photos feed one consistent catalogue look.

Working with AI honestly

Diffusion models are confidently wrong about geometry — the pipeline is designed around verification, keeping the product true while the environment is generated. That discipline transfers to any probabilistic tool.

// catalogue outputs: one visual language across variants
// source: configurator geometry → output: styled catalogue shot
What changed

Catalogue imagery became something the company generates in-house, on demand, in one visual language — instead of a photography budget line.
